report.question: Which prompts, skills, rules, agents and workflow definitions still instruct an agent to call a tool, plugin or command that no longer exists in the live inventory?
report.headline: FIVE artifacts (three distinct, two of them duplicated into a second tree) instruct calls to MCP servers that are absent from the live inventory: skills/knowledge-ops/SKILL.md is the only one with NO guard of any kind (four `Use mcp__memory__*` directives), skills/hacktricks/SKILL.md and the devfleet trio carry file-level fallbacks or an install prerequisite but assert live-inventory facts that are false, and ace-tool / SlopOrNot / openaiDeveloperDocs / Serena degrade gracefully behind guards. The calibration case is CLEAN: all 9 references to the retired AgentBridge budget tools are retirement notices or an unrelated `def check_budget(`, and the disabled-plugin references are notices or the config that performs the disabling -- so the estate's retirement propagation worked. The command/binary half of the specified mechanism found ZERO dead references at 0/10 precision on the targeted set, because instruction artifacts invoke tools by path, by `python -m`, by npx/uvx or on a device, not from PATH -- and a SINGLE-resolver set difference, which is the naive reading of the mechanism, manufactures 25 false positives with Git-Bash alone or 44 with a bulk Get-Command dump alone.

report.answer_to_the_question: Five artifacts, covering three distinct capabilities, instruct calls to MCP servers absent from the live inventory, and exactly ONE of them does so with no guard whatsoever: skills/knowledge-ops/SKILL.md:131-134 (four `Use mcp__memory__*` directives, P2). The devfleet trio (15 sites) is mitigated only by an install prerequisite, and skills/hacktricks/SKILL.md (16 sites) plus skills/orchestration-patterns/SKILL.md (4 sites) keep working fallbacks but assert live-inventory facts that are now false -- stale premises, P3. ace-tool (24 sites), SlopOrNot (8) and openaiDeveloperDocs (5) all degrade behind guards. NOTHING still instructs a retired AgentBridge tool and NOTHING still instructs a disabled plugin: the estate's retirement propagation is clean, and the 9 get_budget/check_budget hits plus the 8 agentbridge/serena hits are notices, guards, or the config that performs the disabling. The command class contributes zero confirmed dead references. The fix in every confirmed case is to edit the INSTRUCTION -- repoint, guard, or delete -- not any call site.
report.probe_1_as_specified: SATISFIED. `extract every tool/command token from instruction artifacts and set-difference it against the live inventory`: 1,938 tracked instruction files / 10,797,307 bytes yielded 72 distinct mcp__ tokens (232 occurrences), 117 plugin@marketplace occurrences, 9 retired-name occurrences and 9,349 command-head tokens; set-differenced against 64 mounted MCP servers (`claude mcp list`), 98 plugins with enabled/disabled state (`claude plugin list`) and Git-Bash `command -v`.
report.probe_2_as_specified: SATISFIED and mechanically different in both halves. Binaries: PowerShell per-name `Get-Command` instead of Git-Bash `command -v` -- and the disagreement is real and measured in BOTH directions, which is why the AND-gate exists (Git-Bash alone: 25 false positives including mon/wfmon, the documented .cmd-shim blindness; a bulk Get-Command dump alone: 44 the other way including grep/sed/awk). MCP names: resolution through the LIVE tool schema via ToolSearch `select:`, which touches no CLI stdout at all; present and absent names were resolved inside the SAME call so the silence is controlled.
report.method_limitations_inline: (1) The mcp__ token shape bounds recall -- a prose instruction naming a dead capability without that shape is invisible, exactly as get_budget was until it was hand-added to a retired set. (2) The marker classifier scores unfenced prose as MENTION, so the UNGUARDED count of 4 is a LOWER BOUND; 23 of 42 such MENTIONs carry an imperative and 3 of those (skills/openai-docs/SKILL.md:13-15) are genuinely unconditional bullets. (3) The command class resolves PATH membership, which is not capability existence; 10/10 of its survivors were false positives. (4) The corpus is the TRACKED repo tree only; docs/, platform/, command-center/ and the untracked live trees are out of scope. (5) `mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate` was a NAME I constructed rather than one taken from an artifact, so its non-resolution is server-level evidence only -- the artifact-derived names carry both server-level and tool-level evidence.
